summary: Geshe Lhundub Sopa (1923–2014) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Ganden Chokhor and Sera Jey monasteries under Lhundrub Thabkhe, Geshe Ngawang Rigsal, Geshe Ngawang Gendun, and Lhundrub Tsöndrü, later serving as a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison.
Geshe Lobsang Tenzin is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held an attested post at Sera Monastery in 1980 and served as abbot of Gyume Tantric College as attested in 1987.

Geshe Lobsang Tharchin (1921–2004) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his studies at Sera Monastery, earning his Lharampa Geshe degree by 1953, and also studied at Gyume Tantric College.

Geshe Losang Chödar is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. In 2010, he held an attested position at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and served as a Tibetan editor at the Institute of Tibetan Classics.

Geshe Ngawang Nyima (1907–1990) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He held a post at Leiden University in 1960 and served at Drepung Monastery, where he was Abbot of Drepung Gomang Monastery.

Geshe Palden Drakpa specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He was a visiting scholar at the University of Virginia in 1987 and served as librarian at Tibet House in New Delhi, attested between 1987 and 2004.

Geshe Sonam Rinchen (1933–2013) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies from circa 1968 to 1971 and served as a teacher at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives from circa 1978 to 2013.

Geshe Tashi Tsering (born 1958) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Sera and Gyuto monasteries, taught at Kopan Monastery and Gandhi Foundation College, and became resident teacher at Jamyang Buddhist Centre in 1994.
Geshe Tsondru Namgyal is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies who earned Geshe degrees through his studies at Drepung Monastery and Yungdrung Ling Monastery.

Geshe Wangyal (1901–1983) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Drepung Monastery under Agvan Dorjiev. He taught at Columbia University (~1967–1974) and the Tibetan Buddhist Learning Center (~1958–1983).

Geshe Yeshe Thabkhe (born 1930) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He held posts as a scholar at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, attested in 1991 and from 2001 to 2019.

Geshe Yeshe Tobden (1926–1999) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sera Monastery under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Geshe Lodoe Sangpo, and Chusang Rinpoche, and taught Buddhist philosophy at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1967–1970).
Gessho Sasaki (1875–1926) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University from circa 1896 to 1900. He subsequently held an academic post at Otani University from circa 1901 to 1926.

Giacomella Orofino is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" and Sapienza University of Rome under Raniero Gnoli, later teaching at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (attested 2000–2007).
Gianpaolo Vetturini is a scholar in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of London under the doctoral supervision of Tadeusz Skorupski.

Giei Honda (1888–1953) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. After studying at Kyoto University, he served as a professeur adjoint there from 1934 to 1948 and also held a post at Rissho University.

Gikyo Ito (1909–1996) specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at Kyoto University under Atsuuji Ashikaga and held posts at Osaka University of Foreign Studies and Kyoto Sangyo University.

Gil Fronsdal (born 1954) is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned a PhD at Stanford University (~1989–1998) and held posts at the Sati Center for Buddhist Studies (~1997) and Insight Meditation Center (~2001).

Gilles Tarabout is an Indology and religious studies scholar. In 2004, he was attested as a senior fellow at CNRS, a member at EHESS, and an exchange program director at Fondation Maison des Sciences de l'Homme.
Gin Ling Liu is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Hong Kong under doctoral supervisor Jing Yin and also studied under Hsing Yun, attested in 2008.
